sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ever wondered why some string operations in Java are slow? Let's fix that!

• Why regular strings can be inefficient
• How StringBuilder and StringBuffer make string operations faster
• When to use each one (they're not the same!)

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine you're building a LEGO tower. With regular strings, every time you add a block, you have to:
1. Take a photo of your current tower
2. Build a new tower with the extra block
3. Throw away the old tower

That's how regular String concatenation works - it creates new objects every time!

StringBuilder and StringBuffer are like having a reusable LEGO board where you can just keep adding blocks without starting over.

• **StringBuilder**: Your personal LEGO board (not thread-safe, but fast)
• **StringBuffer**: A shared LEGO board with safety locks (thread-safe, slightly slower)
• Both let you modify strings without creating new objects each time

sections.title: Code Examples
examples:
StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder("Hello");
sb.append(" World");        // "Hello World"
sb.insert(5, ",");          // "Hello, World"
sb.delete(5, 6);            // "Hello World"
sb.reverse();               // "dlroW olleH"
sb.replace(0, 5, "Java");   // "Java olleH"

System.out.println(sb.toString());
System.out.println(sb.length());     // length
System.out.println(sb.capacity());   // capacity

sections.title: Key Points
points: StringBuilder is a mutable alternative to String for efficient string modification
append() adds text to the end; insert() adds text at a specified position
delete() and deleteCharAt() remove characters; reverse() reverses the entire sequence
StringBuilder is more efficient than String concatenation in loops
StringBuffer is thread-safe but slower; StringBuilder is preferred for single-threaded code

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: StringBuilder = fast string modifications (single-threaded) StringBuffer = thread-safe version (multi-threaded) Use append(), insert(), delete() for modifications. Convert to String with toString() when done. Ready to optimize your string operations.
